area: settings (sequencer, science, phd2-guiding, plate-solving, weather-safety, notifications + all transports, integrations/plugins, annotations, observation log, auto-save, cloud-sync)

units_unreached.unit: screen:settings/notification_routing_settings.dart -> _HomeAssistantSection (tail of the Notifications page, below MQTT broker)
units_unreached.why: The Notifications page is ~3000px of scroll; I enumerated it down through the MQTT broker section and ran out of budget before the final Home Assistant routing block. Home Assistant WAS reached from the other direction (Settings > Integrations > Home Assistant > Configure), so the transport is covered but this specific routing section's controls were not operated.

Fields were enumerated and one (Topic) was edited live, but I did not press 'Save MQTT config' / 'Test MQTT'. The other six transports' Test buttons were all exercised and all behaved honestly, so I have no reason to suspect MQTT differs -- but I did not verify it.

findings.title: Per-event routing claims it will deliver to Email/Telegram/MQTT that the same page knows are unconfigured
findings.what_happened: In Per-event routing I opened Edit on 'Sequence Paused' and selected the Email (SMTP), Telegram and MQTT transport chips. All three highlighted with a tick, with no warning of any kind. After Save the list row reads '> In-app banner + Email (SMTP) + Telegram + MQTT'. Nothing is configured: no SMTP host, no Telegram bot token, no MQTT broker. The very same page's 'Send test' for email answers 'Failed: Email is not configured' -- so the app HAS the knowledge and does not use it in the routing UI. DB confirms the write: notification_routing_matrix -> "sequencePaused":{"transports":["inApp","email","telegram","mqtt"],...}
findings.expected: Unconfigured transports should be disabled (or chip-labelled 'not configured') in the editor, and the summary line should mark them, e.g. '> In-app banner + Email (not configured)'. A user arming alerts before an unattended night is being told three channels will reach them when none will.
findings.repro: Settings (gear) > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications > scroll to 'Per-event routing' > 'Sequence Paused' > Edit > click Email (SMTP), Telegram, MQTT > Save. Read the row subtitle. Then scroll further down and press 'Send test' under Email (SMTP).
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-38-routing-transports.png (all three chips ticked, no warning), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-39-routing-saved.png (summary line), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-46-smtp-test.png ('Failed: Email is not configured'); sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/settings-obs/data/skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='notification_routing_matrix'"
findings.proposed_fix: Give the routing matrix a per-transport 'configured' predicate (SMTP host non-empty, telegram bot token present in keyring, mqtt broker host non-empty, discord/pushover secrets present) and use it in two places: disable/annotate the chip in _CategoryEditorDialog, and render the summary as '<label> (not configured)' in _categoryRow.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end-to-end on display :83 / profile settings-obs-verify. Settings > Notifications > Per-event routing > Sequence Paused > Edit: the transport FilterChips render from NotificationTransportKind.values with no configured-state gating (packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/notification_routing_settings/category_editor_dialog.dart:83-100) — I ticked Email (SMTP), Telegram and MQTT and got no warning (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-24-crop.png). After Save the row subtitle reads exactly '-> In-app banner + Email (SMTP) + Telegram + MQTT' (shot sov-25-crop.png, and the AT-SPI tree returns the same string), built by notification_routing_settings.dart:166-168 which the finding cites correctly. sqlite3 on the scratch DB confirms the write: notification_routing_matrix sequencePaused.transports = [inApp, email, telegram, mqtt]. The consequence follows and is worse than a cosmetic label: notification_router.dart:485-498 (_eligibleTransports) silently DROPS any transport whose isConfigured is false at send time, so nothing is delivered and nothing is logged. The same page does hold the knowledge — router.sendTest returns NotificationResult.fail('<name> is not configured') (notification_router.dart:279-281) and the Email 'Send test' button surfaced a red failure indicator when I pressed it with an empty SMTP host. P1 is correct: this is the arm-alerts-before-an-unattended-night path and the app asserts three channels will reach the operator when none will.

findings.title: Two independent Discord (and two Pushover) configurations on the same page; filling one leaves the other's Test saying it is unconfigured
findings.what_happened: The Notifications page has a 'Discord' section near the top (Webhook URL + Test Discord) and a 'Discord (routing matrix)' section ~2000px lower (Webhook URL + Username override + Save + Test). They are separate stores. I pasted https://discord.com/api/webhooks/111/AUDITMATRIX into the routing-matrix one and saved -- toast 'Discord (routing) saved', field became '******** (stored securely)' with Replace/Clear. I then scrolled back up: the top 'Discord' section's Webhook URL was still the empty placeholder, and its 'Test Discord' answered 'Please enter a Discord webhook URL'. The identical duplication exists for Pushover ('Pushover' with API Key/User Key/Test vs 'Pushover (routing matrix)' with API token/User key/Device/Save/Test).
findings.expected: One Discord configuration per page. A user who configures Discord anywhere on the Notifications page should not be told by another control on that same page that Discord is unconfigured. If the legacy rows must survive for the legacy push path, they need to read from the same secret and be labelled as such.
findings.repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications. Scroll to 'Discord (routing matrix)', paste any webhook URL, press 'Save Discord config'. Scroll back up to the 'Discord' section and press 'Test Discord'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-52-discord-saved.png (routing matrix saved, masked), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-56-legacy-discord4.png (top Discord section still empty), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-57-legacy-discord-test.png ('Please enter a Discord webhook URL'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-47-tr-2.png (duplicate Pushover). DB: app_settings discord_webhook='' while notification_transport_discord={"webhookUrl":"",...} with the URL in the keyring.
findings.proposed_fix: Delete the legacy Discord/Pushover rows from notification_settings.dart and migrate discord_webhook / pushover_key / pushover_user into the keyring-backed transport config on first run (the same one-shot migration pattern already used by secrets_store.dart's notification_secrets_migrated_v2). If they must stay, retitle them 'Discord (legacy push)' and have both read the same source.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. On one scroll of the Notifications page I see 'Discord' (Webhook URL + Test Discord) at notification_settings.dart:587-623 reading settings.discordWebhook, and 'Discord (routing matrix)' at notification_routing_settings/discord_transport_section.dart:34/64 backed by the keyring transport config — plus the identical pair for 'Pushover' (notification_settings.dart:624-677) vs 'Pushover (routing matrix)' (pushover_transport_section.dart:37/80). The duplication is deliberate per the in-source comment at notification_settings.dart:678-683 ('separate keys to keep legacy NotificationService working unchanged'), but nothing in the UI says so. Live contradiction on ONE page: the routing-matrix Discord webhook showed '******** (stored securely)' with Replace/Clear (shot sov-30-disc2.png) while the top 'Discord' section's Webhook URL was the empty grey hint, and pressing its 'Test' produced the orange toast 'Please enter a Discord webhook URL' (shot sov-34-crop.png). Confirmed. I am lowering P1 -> P2: unlike finding #1 nothing is silently dropped on a path the user armed — both halves work in isolation, the harm is a duplicated/contradictory config surface. (Incidental, worth its own item: the routing-matrix secret was already present on a --fresh profile, i.e. the keyring is not scoped by SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR and leaks across audit profiles.)

findings.title: Auto-Save Status reports 'Last backup: Never' while a backup from 20 minutes earlier in the same session exists and is listed on another settings page
findings.what_happened: Fresh profile launched 13:54:14Z. At 14:19Z the Status card read 'Last backup: Never' with trailing state 'Pending'. At that exact moment app_settings held autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-01T13:59:15.750118Z, and Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore listed seven real bundles (skotiq_autosave_2026-08-01T09-59-20 ... T10-09-50 local) which also exist on disk in ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups/. After pressing 'Back Up Now' the same card immediately read '0s ago / In 23h', and later '18m ago / In 23h' -- so the widget only shows backups it observed after subscribing, and never hydrates the persisted timestamp.
findings.expected: 'Last backup: 20m ago'. Telling an operator their database has NEVER been backed up when it was backed up 20 minutes ago is the kind of false negative that makes people either panic-export or stop trusting the field.
findings.repro: Start the app on a fresh profile. Wait ~5 min for the startup auto-backup. Open Settings > Files & Storage > scroll to AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS > Status. Compare with `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select value from app_settings where key='autosave.last_backup_at'"` and with Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore > Recent Backups.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-60-autosave.png and settings-obs-61-savenow.png ('Never' / 'Pending'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-62-backupnow.png ('0s ago' after manual backup), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-81-testconn2.png (Recent Backups list, 7 bundles from 09:59-10:20), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-92-autosave-recheck.png ('18m ago')
findings.proposed_fix: The hydrating provider already exists -- packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/auto_save_service.dart:745-780 defines an autoSaveStatusStream that back-fills lastBackup from the persisted _lastBackupKey. Have _AutoSaveSettingsState watch that provider instead of ref.read(autoSaveServiceProvider).status / .statusStream.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently on a fresh profile. Profile launched 14:48:29Z; the startup auto-backup ran at 14:53:25Z (app_settings autosave.last_backup_at = 2026-08-01T14:53:25.161687Z, and ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups/skotiq_autosave_2026-08-01T10-53-25.082618.nsbackup exists on disk). At 14:56Z Settings > Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS > Status still read 'Last backup / Never' with trailing 'Pending' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-04-autosave2.png). The named cause is right: _AutoSaveSettingsState.initState reads ref.read(autoSaveServiceProvider).status and subscribes to .statusStream (auto_save_settings.dart:41-56), which never back-fills the persisted key. The strongest evidence is an in-app contradiction the finding only half-states: Settings > ADVANCED > Backup & Restore on the SAME running instance showed 'Last Full Backup: Aug 1, 2026 10:53' (shot sov-39-backuprestore.png) because backup_screen.dart:432 watches autoSaveStatusProvider — the hydrating provider at auto_save_service.dart:762 that the finding points at (it names it 'autoSaveStatusStream'; the actual identifier is autoSaveStatusProvider, doc comment at 745-761 — a naming slip, not a defect in the claim). The proposed fix is exactly the pattern already used by the sibling screen. Lowering P1 -> P2: it is a display-only false negative on one of two surfaces; no data is lost and no night is at risk.

findings.title: Editing a settings dropdown fires a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' alert on a completely idle app, and the alert text contradicts itself
findings.what_happened: With no devices connected, no run active and the app sitting on the Settings screen, flipping Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON (and separately Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)') immediately raised a red CRITICAL toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.' An earlier variant also appended 'NO MOUNT CONNECTED -- nothing was parked; if a mount is ...'. Two problems: (1) a rig-SAFING event is being raised by a settings edit while nothing is running; (2) 'Rig safed' and 'no action was possible' are contradictory claims in one sentence -- nothing was safed because nothing was connected. I monitored for 5.5 minutes afterwards with fail-closed armed and it did NOT repeat, so this is a one-shot per state transition, not a flood.
findings.expected: Changing a policy in Settings should surface an informational/warning disclosure ('Weather safety is on but no weather source is connected -- runs will park and abort with the current fail mode'), not a red CRITICAL safing alert. And the wording must not say the rig was safed when the app's own text says no action was possible.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety > toggle 'Enable weather safety' ON. Screenshot within ~2s. Then Settings > Sequencer > 'Safety fail mode' > 'Fail Closed (Park)'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-07-ws-enabled.png (first, truncated variant), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png (full text: 'Safe the rig / CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible.'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-88-watch-1..6.png (no repeat over 5.5 min)
findings.proposed_fix: Gate the SafeRig escalation on there being something to safe (a run in progress or a connected mount/dome); otherwise emit a warning-severity disclosure. And when detail resolves to 'no action was possible', drop the 'Rig safed:' lead-in entirely -- say 'Nothing to safe: no mount or dome connected.'
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced verbatim. Nothing connected (Camera/Mount/Guider all Disconnected), no run active, app parked on the Settings screen. Toggling Weather Safety > 'Enable weather safety' ON raised, within 2s, a red toast titled 'Safe the rig' reading 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is ...' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-06-ws-on.png). Both cited locations are exact: safe_rig_service.dart:504 is literally `'CRITICAL: $reason. Rig safed: $detail.$gap'` with detail defaulting to 'no action was possible' at :498, and weather_safety_provider.dart:625-700 is the no-data fail-mode path that resolves to unsafe/shouldPark. It is not merely a message: the app log recorded 'Secondary rig stopped' at 2026-08-01T14:57:23Z, i.e. the safing routine really executed off a settings edit on an idle app. The self-contradiction ('Rig safed: no action was possible') is real. P2 is right - one-shot per state transition, no repeat, no equipment at risk here, but it trains operators to ignore the one alert class that must never be ignored.

findings.title: Bundled plugins show a green 'Enabled' pill with zero configuration; Home Assistant Configure saves an entirely empty config silently
findings.what_happened: On a fresh profile Settings > Integrations shows all four plugins -- Discord Webhook, Pushover Notification, Home Assistant, Weather Logger -- with a green dot and a tick reading 'Enabled', although none has any configuration. I opened Home Assistant > Configure, left Base URL and Long-lived access token completely empty, and pressed Save: the dialog closed with no validation error, no toast, and the row still read 'Enabled'. Querying the DB afterwards, no Home Assistant keys exist at all (select key,value from app_settings where key like '%home%' or key like '%assistant%' returns nothing). I then toggled the Discord Webhook plugin off: the pill changed to a grey 'Disabled', proving the pill tracks the enable flag only and never reflects configuration.
findings.expected: Either 'Enabled -- not configured' with a warning colour, or Save should refuse an empty Base URL. The Backup & Sync panel on another page does exactly the right thing ('Server URL is required.'), so the pattern already exists in this codebase.
findings.repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Integrations. Observe all four pills. Click Configure on Home Assistant, leave both fields empty, click Save. Observe the row is unchanged. Toggle Discord Webhook's switch off to see the pill respond only to the switch.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-40-integrations.png (four green 'Enabled' pills, nothing configured), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-41-ha-config.png (empty dialog), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-42-ha-save-empty.png (saved silently, pill unchanged), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-43-plugin-off.png (pill flips to 'Disabled' on the switch)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a per-plugin isConfigured() and render three states in the pill (Disabled / Enabled - not configured / Enabled). In home_assistant_config_dialog.dart validate baseUrl non-empty + parseable and token non-empty before Save, and show the same red snackbar style the cloud-sync panel uses.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The load-bearing claim is false. home_assistant_config_dialog.dart:53-62 already validates: `if (baseUrl.isEmpty || token.isEmpty) { _validationError = 'Both the base URL and a long-lived access token are required.'; return; }` — and the built bundle contains it (lib/libapp.so built Aug 1 09:42; the file's last commit c66c60f71 is Jul 26 and is an ancestor of HEAD). I reproduced the auditor's observation first (Save closed the dialog, no error) and then found why: the fields were NOT empty. Skotiq's PluginStorage is a JSON file under $HOME, NOT under SKOTIQ_DATA_DIR (plugin_context.dart:326 _defaultPluginStorageDirectory), and ~/.local/share/skotiq/skotiq_plugins/storage/com.skotiq.examples.home_assistant.json already contained {"home_assistant.baseUrl":"http://homeassistant.local:8123","home_assistant.token":"token-abc"}. The dialog was prefilled — the URL was bright value text, and the 9 dots in the token field were 'token-abc' obscured, not a placeholder. When I cleared both fields (shot sov-15-crop.png shows dim hint text in both) and pressed Save, the dialog STAYED OPEN and rendered the exact red message the finding says is missing (shot sov-16-crop.png). The supporting DB query is also misdirected: HA config never goes to app_settings, so 'no home/assistant keys' proves nothing. The residual pill claim does not survive either — the auditor's HA and Pushover plugins were in fact configured, Discord's credential is per-NODE by design ('An empty default is allowed (each node can still carry its own URL)', discord_config_dialog.dart:56-58), and Weather Logger takes no configuration, so a 'not configured' pill would itself be the untrue statement. Real incidental issue surfaced by this: plugin storage and the OS keyring escape the audit profile sandbox, which is what manufactured this false positive.

findings.title: Raw Dart StateError text leaks into a user-facing error toast
findings.what_happened: Pressing 'Test' on 'Test push notification' with no remote access running produced the toast: 'Failed to send test notification: Bad state: No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' The 'Bad state:' prefix is StateError.toString() bleeding through into shipped copy.
findings.expected: 'Failed to send test notification: no push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' The message content is good and actionable -- only the exception prefix is wrong.
findings.repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications > scroll to 'Push to Mobile' > 'Test push notification' > Test.
findings.where: notification test-push handler in packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/settings/widgets/notification_settings.dart (catch block interpolating the raw error)
findings.proposed_fix: Catch StateError specifically and surface e.message, or strip the 'Bad state: ' prefix before interpolating.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced exactly. Settings > Notifications > Push to Mobile > 'Test push notification' > Test produced the red toast 'Failed to send test notification: Bad state: No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' (shot /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-20-testpush.png). Source path matches: push_notification_service.dart:182-186 throws StateError('No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.') and notification_settings.dart:197 interpolates the object with `'Failed to send test notification: $e'`, so StateError.toString()'s 'Bad state: ' prefix reaches shipped copy. P3 is right — cosmetic, the message is otherwise accurate and actionable.

findings.title: 'Re-scan now' on Plate Solving gives no feedback whatsoever
findings.what_happened: The Plate Solving page's step-3 card says 'Once ASTAP and the catalog are installed, click Re-scan so Skotiq picks them up' and offers 'Re-scan now' (there is a second 'Re-scan' button below the card). Clicking it produced no spinner, no toast, no change of any kind on screen, and no new line in the app log. Since the correct answer (ASTAP still not installed) was already displayed, the user has no way to tell whether the button did anything at all -- which is exactly the situation where someone installs ASTAP, clicks Re-scan, sees nothing happen, and concludes the app is broken.
findings.expected: A brief spinner on the button plus a result toast ('No plate solver found' / 'Found ASTAP at /usr/bin/astap'). The provider already has a `rescanning` flag (PlateSolverSettingsState.rescanning) that nothing appears to render on this control.
findings.repro: Settings > IMAGING/search 'plate' > Plate Solving > 'Re-scan now'. Compare the before/after screenshots and `drive_linux.py log --tail 30`.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-64-platesolving.png and /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-65-rescan.png are pixel-identical apart from the clock; app log shows nothing for the interval
findings.proposed_fix: Bind the buttons' loading state to uiState.rescanning and show a result snackbar from the awaited plateSolverDetectionProvider refresh.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Does not reproduce, and the source claim is wrong on both counts. I clicked 'Re-scan now' and captured a burst of screenshots instead of one: at ~0.8s and ~1.5s after the click a green snackbar reads 'Re-scanned plate-solver paths.' at the bottom of the window (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/sov-37-bot-0.8.png, sov-37-bot-1.5.png); it is absent at ~0.3s (detect() has not returned yet) and gone again by the later frame. A single before/after pair taken outside that ~1s-to-~4s window is pixel-identical, which is precisely the evidence the finding presents. The claim that nothing renders `rescanning` is also false: plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:675-678 renders `label: isRescanning ? 'Re-scanning...' : 'Re-scan now'` with `isLoading: isRescanning`, the second button does the same at :375-379, and _rescan() at :239-253 already shows showSuccessSnackBar('Re-scanned plate-solver paths.') / showErrorSnackBar('Re-scan failed: $e'). The proposed fix is already implemented. (Fair residual nit, well below P3: the success copy does not state the RESULT — 'No plate solver found' vs a path — but the finding as written is refuted.)

findings.title: Dead/duplicated settings keys persist and are exported while no UI reflects them
findings.what_happened: Two cases found by diffing the UI against the scratch DB. (1) app_settings.auto_save_sequences = 'true' (its shipped default) coexists with autosave.sequence_enabled = 'false', which is what the Files & Storage toggle showed and what AutoSaveService actually obeys. No UI surfaces auto_save_sequences, but it is written into settings snapshots/exports and served through the app-settings model, so a remote/web surface reading it reports sequence auto-save ON while the desktop has it OFF. (2) app_settings.plate_solver = 'ASTAP' coexists with the Plate Solving page's 'Active solver' radio (Auto-fallback), which is backed by Rust platesolver.json via plateSolverPreferenceProvider. Confusingly the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite -- I typed 45 into Timeout and plate_solve_timeout went 60 -> 45 -- so one page writes two different stores.
findings.expected: One store per logical setting. Anything that rides export/backup/API should be the value the app actually obeys.
findings.repro: Fresh profile. Settings > Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS: 'Enable sequence auto-save' reads OFF. Then `sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db "select key,value from app_settings where key like '%auto_save%' or key like 'autosave%'"`. Same for plate_solver vs the Active solver radio.
findings.evidence: sqlite output: auto_save_sequences|true alongside autosave.sequence_enabled|false; plate_solver|ASTAP alongside a UI showing Auto-fallback. /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-59-files.png (toggle OFF), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-67-verify.png (Auto-fallback selected). Export path is source-only.
findings.proposed_fix: Either delete auto_save_sequences / plate_solver from default_settings.dart and the snapshot mapping, or make the AppSettings getters read through to autosave.sequence_enabled and the Rust platesolver preference so the exported value is the obeyed value.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Case (1) confirmed. My fresh profile's DB holds auto_save_sequences|true while the Files & Storage 'Enable sequence auto-save' toggle reads OFF (shot sov-02-files.png; AutoSaveConfig.sequenceEnabled defaults false and autosave.sequence_enabled is unset). setAutoSaveSequences exists (settings_sections/general.dart:27-30) but grep across packages/skotiq_app/lib finds ZERO callers, and nothing reads state.autoSaveSequences for behaviour — yet app_settings_stored_snapshot_mapping.dart:515 rewrites it on every settings save and BackupService._exportSettings (backup_service.dart:711-715) dumps the whole app_settings table into every .nsbackup. So it is a dead key that is persisted and exported. Case (2) confirmed as a two-store split: plate_solver|ASTAP lives in sqlite with no UI, while the page's Active-solver control is backed by plateSolverPreferenceProvider -> Rust platesolver.json (plate_solver_provider.dart:18-25), and the Solve Parameters on that same page DO write sqlite (plate_solve_parameters_section.dart:87-88 setPlateSolveTimeout; my DB shows plate_solve_timeout|60). TWO CORRECTIONS to the finding's reasoning. (a) The stated consequence for case 1 is unsupported: autoSaveSequences appears nowhere in models/settings/app_settings.dart or app_settings_remote_mapping.dart, so no remote/web surface serves it — the exposure is backup/export files only. (b) 'plate_solver' is NOT dead: default_science_backend/helpers.dart:663-666 _resolveSolverId() returns settings.plateSolver, and app_settings_remote_mapping.dart:651-652 lets a remote client set it — which makes the split arguably a real correctness bug (science labels solves 'ASTAP' while the actual engine preference is auto-fallback), not just tidy-up. Keeping P3.

findings.title: Fail-closed is the shipped default and the Weather Safety page never tells a sensorless rig what that means
findings.what_happened: safety_fail_mode defaults to failClosed (verified in the fresh DB and at app_settings.dart:82). 'Enable weather safety' correctly defaults OFF -- but the moment a user turns it on, which reads like the responsible thing to do, a rig with no weather device and no safety monitor is treated as unsafe: the app raises a CRITICAL 'Safe the rig', and per the codebase's own WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts'. The Weather Safety page itself contains NO fail-mode control, NO row showing which weather sources are connected or what they currently read, and NO hint that zero sources are attached. The fail-mode dropdown lives on a different page (Sequencer). The rule's resolution hint literally says 'switch the safety fail mode to fail open in Settings > Automation & Safety' -- a string the user only meets at run-start, not on the page where they made the choice.
findings.expected: The page that owns the master switch should show live source state and the fail-mode consequence. Concretely: a status row at the top ('Weather sources: none connected -- with Fail Closed, runs will park and abort'), the fail-mode selector moved next to the master switch, and turning the master switch on with zero sources should either default that rig to Warn Only or ask.
findings.repro: Fresh profile, nothing connected. Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety. Read the whole page (3 toggles, 3 thresholds, 2 alert-timing numbers) -- nothing mentions sources or fail mode. Toggle 'Enable weather safety' on. Then go to Sequencer to find 'Safety fail mode: Fail Closed (Park)'.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-06-weather-safety.png and settings-obs-09-ws-scrolled.png (full page, no source/fail-mode info), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-11-sequencer.png (fail mode lives here), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-87-failclosed-toast.png; DB safety_fail_mode|failClosed
findings.proposed_fix: Add a source-status SettingRow driven by weatherStateProvider/safetyMonitorStateProvider at the top of WeatherSafetySettings, move the SafetyFailMode dropdown onto that page (mirroring it in Sequencer the way auto-park is already mirrored), and when weatherSafetyEnabled flips true with no live source, present a one-time choice rather than a CRITICAL toast.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end on a fresh v-misc profile with nothing connected. (1) Default verified two ways: app_settings.dart:82 is `@Default(SafetyFailMode.failClosed) SafetyFailMode safetyFailMode`, and the fresh scratch DB row reads `safety_fail_mode|failClosed`. (2) 'Enable weather safety' does default OFF -- weather_settings.dart:48 `@Default(false)` and weather_settings_dao.dart:33/150 explicitly insert `weatherSafetyEnabled: const Value(false)`; the live page rendered the switch off. (3) The page really is only 3 toggles + 3 thresholds + 2 alert-timing numbers: the live AT-SPI tree lists exactly Enable weather safety / Auto-park mount / Auto-resume after clear / Max humidity / Max wind speed / Max cloud cover / Alert distance / Lead time and nothing else -- no source row, no fail-mode control, no indication that zero weather sources are attached. Confirmed against the full 268-line widget source too. (4) The fail-mode selector really is on another page: `safetyFailMode` appears in exactly one app file, sequencer_settings.dart:569-572, and typing 'Safety fail' into the live Settings search returns one hit, 'Sequencer'. (5) The consequence reproduces: toggling 'Enable weather safety' on with no weather device and no safety monitor fired a CRITICAL notification within seconds -- title 'Safe the rig', body 'CRITICAL: No weather data sources available. Rig safed: no action was possible. NO MOUNT CONNECTED - nothing was parked; if a mount is tracking under another program it is still exposed.' The Rust log shows 'Secondary rig stopped' at the same instant, so SafeRigService actually executed. The cited file:line is accurate (weather_safety_settings.dart:123-175 is the SettingsPage / Safety Actions block, master switch at 133-143). Severity corrected P1 -> P2: the finding's framing ('invisible until it fires', 'the run will park and abort shortly after it starts') overstates what ships. WeatherSafetyNoSourceRule is registered in the pre-flight validator (sequence_validation.dart:348) at ValidationSeverity.error, and every start path throws SequenceValidationException on any error-severity issue (sequence_validation.dart:474-493), so this configuration BLOCKS the run before it starts rather than aborting it after a slew, with a message carrying the exact resolution hint. Combined with the master switch defaulting off and the loud CRITICAL toast fired the instant it is turned on, the operator is not silently doomed. The real, remaining defect is disclosure: the page owning the master switch shows neither the fail mode nor the absence of sources, and the CRITICAL toast never says 'fail mode' or where to change it.

findings.title: PHD2 Guiding settings has no way to test the connection -- the one integration you cannot verify
findings.what_happened: The entire PHD2 Guiding page is Host, Port, 'PHD2 executable path (Auto-detect, optional)' and a paragraph of prose. There is no Connect/Test button, no live PHD2 connection state, no PHD2 version readout, no PHD2 profile selector, no 'launch PHD2 if not running', and no 'connect equipment in PHD2 on start'. Every other integration in this app can be verified from its settings page -- SMTP/Discord/Pushover/Telegram/generic-webhook all have 'Send test', cloud sync has 'Test Connection', both plate solvers have 'Verify', and the plate solving page even shows 'Auto-detect -- not found' inline. PHD2 is the most failure-prone dependency in the whole stack and is the only one with no verification affordance.
findings.expected: A 'Test connection' button that opens the PHD2 event socket and reports version + current profile + connected state, and an inline auto-detect status for the executable path matching the Plate Solving page's 'Auto-detect -- not found' pattern. NINA shows PHD2's state and version inline on its guider page.
findings.repro: Settings > search 'PHD2' > PHD2 Guiding. Read the whole page.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-73-phd2.png (whole page fits on one screen with room to spare); contrast /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-66-ps-1.png (Plate Solving's Verify + auto-detect status) and settings-obs-79-sync-1.png (cloud sync's Test Connection)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a Test row that calls the existing PHD2 client's connect/get-version RPC against the configured host:port and renders success (version, active profile) or the socket error, plus an auto-detect status subtitle on the executable path row reusing the plate-solver detection pattern.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The literal claim reproduces. The live AT-SPI tree of Settings > PHD2 Guiding lists exactly: Host, Port, PHD2 executable path ('Auto-detect (optional)' / 'Not set'), and the Information paragraph -- no Test/Connect button, no connection state, no version, no profile selector, matching the full 209-line source. The 'Not set' subtitle is only a reflection of an empty phd2Path, not a probe result, so the contrast is fair: plate_solving_settings_screen.dart:390/403/441 do render 'Auto-detect - not found' from a live detection, and Send test / Test Connection do exist in transport_controls.dart and cloud_sync_settings.dart. BUT the headline rationale -- 'the one integration you cannot verify', 'the only one with no verification affordance' -- is false, and I refuted it in the running app. (a) The Guiding screen header shows live 'PHD2 Disconnected' with a Connect button; clicking it raised a toast titled 'PHD2' reading 'PHD2 not running - searching for installed PHD2...', which is phd2_launcher.dart:99. Phd2Launcher does exactly what the finding says does not exist: launches the configured executable (or calls apiLaunchPhd2 when the path is blank), then polls host:port until it opens, with distinct errors for 'executable not found', 'failed to launch' and 'launched but did not open port'. (b) Onboarding > Guider already has the requested affordance: a 'Test' button calling GuidingBackend.isPhd2Running(host, port) rendering 'PHD2 reachable at <host:port>. Selection saved.' or 'No response on <host:port>. Is PHD2 running with "Enable Server" turned on?' (guider_step.dart:73-121, 234-245), persisting phd2Host/phd2Port on success. Surviving sub-claims: no PHD2 version readout anywhere, and no profile selector -- the bridge exposes api_phd2_get_profile (native .../api/phd2.rs:749) but apiPhd2GetProfile has zero Dart callers outside the generated binding, so that is dead capability rather than shipped UI. Severity corrected P1 -> P3: a parity/discoverability gap on one settings page for a capability that already exists two clicks away, not an unverifiable integration and not a risk to an observing night. Not a duplicate of the other finding in this batch.
findings.location_wrong: File is right (phd2_guiding_settings.dart, all 209 lines) but two of the enumerated missing items are wrong: 'no live PHD2 connection state' and 'no launch PHD2 if not running' both already exist, on the Guiding screen (guiding_screen_parts/desktop_sections.dart:82-85,219 and services/phd2_launcher.dart). A fixer acting on the finding as written would rebuild Phd2Launcher and the onboarding tester.

findings.title: 'Audible alert on critical events' is OFF by default inside the section titled 'Critical events (unattended imaging)'
findings.what_happened: Under the heading 'Critical events (unattended imaging)', 'Audible alert on critical events -- Play the system bell when a critical error fires' ships OFF. The sibling 'Push critical alerts to mobile' ships ON but honestly discloses that it delivers nothing until remote access is configured. So on a fresh install the section whose entire purpose is reaching an absent operator has zero working channels, and the one that needs no setup at all is the one turned off.
findings.expected: Default the system bell ON. It costs nothing, needs no configuration, and is the only channel that works out of the box on a laptop sitting next to the rig. If the concern is nuisance during attended imaging, gate it on 'a sequence is running' rather than defaulting it off.
findings.repro: Fresh profile. Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications > 'Critical events (unattended imaging)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Flip the shipped default for the audible critical alert to true.

findings.title: 'Use TNS sandbox' defaults OFF -- a first-time submission goes straight to the production Transient Name Server
findings.what_happened: Settings > Science > Transient Name Server (TNS) provides Bot id, Bot name, Reporting group id, Data source id, Reporter name, Bot API key, and 'Use TNS sandbox -- Submit to the TNS sandbox instead of production (no public record)', which is OFF on a fresh profile. A user who fills in their bot credentials and submits a discovery therefore posts a public, permanent AT record to the real TNS on their very first attempt, with no confirmation step and no dry-run.
findings.expected: Sandbox ON by default. Require an explicit opt-out (ideally after one successful sandbox submission) before the app can write to production TNS. Submitting a bogus transient to the public registry is not something you can quietly undo, and the cost of the safe default is one toggle.
findings.repro: Fresh profile. Settings > SCIENCE > Science > scroll to 'Transient Name Server (TNS)'.
findings.proposed_fix: Default tnsUseSandbox to true and add a confirmation dialog on the first switch to production.

findings.title: The Notifications page is one ~3000px scroll with transport config 2500px below where you select it, and three duplicate ways to say the same thing
findings.what_happened: Top-to-bottom the page is: General, Notification Events, Critical events, Push to Mobile (+Test), Discord (legacy), Pushover (legacy), Routing master switch, ~25 per-event routing rows, Email (SMTP), Generic webhook, Pushover (routing matrix), Telegram, Discord (routing matrix), MQTT broker, Home Assistant. Selecting 'Email (SMTP)' as a routing transport near the top gives no link to the SMTP fields far below. Meanwhile 'Sequence complete' and 'Errors' under Notification Events duplicate 'Sequence completed' and 'Sequence failed' under Push to Mobile, which duplicate the 'Sequence Completed'/'Sequence Failed' rows in Per-event routing -- three separate controls for one intent, with no explanation of precedence. Reaching MQTT from the top took nine wheel-scroll batches.
findings.expected: Split transports onto their own settings leaf (or tabs: Events | Routing | Transports), and make the transport chips in the routing dialog link to their config. Collapse the three duplicate event lists into the routing matrix, which is the general case.
findings.repro: Settings > NOTIFICATIONS & REMOTE > Notifications and scroll from top to bottom.
findings.proposed_fix: Register 'Notification transports' as its own settings leaf in settings_catalog.dart and have _CategoryEditorDialog's chips deep-link into it.

findings.title: Science 'Show advanced overlay controls' (off) and 'Science overlays' (on) both promise PSF/residual layers with no disclosure that one gates the other
findings.what_happened: Two adjacent switches in the Mode section: 'Show advanced overlay controls -- Adds PSF, residual, and tile-map layers to the Imaging overlays menu' (ships OFF) and 'Science overlays -- Enable overlays such as PSF map, residual vectors, and tracks' (ships ON). They are independent booleans (advancedModeEnabled / overlayEnabled) whose subtitles name the same three artefacts. The shipped state therefore reads 'Science overlays: ON' while the control that exposes them is hidden, and neither row mentions the other.
findings.expected: This app already solved this exact problem one page away: the Weather Safety rows append '-- inactive until "Enable weather safety" is on' when the master switch is off. Do the same here, or collapse the pair into one switch plus a sub-option.
findings.repro: Fresh profile. Settings > SCIENCE > Science > Mode.
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse the _withPrerequisite() helper pattern from weather_safety_settings.dart:73-77 for the dependent row.

findings.title: Weather Safety carries three hardware thresholds that are inert without a sensor, and no debounce/hysteresis anywhere
findings.what_happened: The Hardware Thresholds section offers Max humidity 90%, Max wind speed 30 km/h and Max cloud cover 80% with subtitles like 'Pause when sensor humidity exceeds this value'. On a rig with no weather device -- the exact rig the fail-closed default punishes -- all three are inert, and the page never says so. Separately, the page has no debounce, no 'N consecutive unsafe readings', and no 'wait N minutes after conditions clear before resuming'; the only timing controls are radar-alert distance (30 km) and lead time (15 min), which are about the cloud-radar API rather than the hardware gate. A single spurious humidity spike therefore trips the whole gate.
findings.expected: Grey out or annotate the threshold rows when no weather device is connected, and add an unsafe-debounce (consecutive readings or seconds) plus a resume-delay. NINA and SGP both expose these; without them the thresholds are all-or-nothing.
findings.repro: Settings > AUTOMATION & SAFETY > Weather Safety, full page.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-09-ws-scrolled.png (whole page: 3 toggles, 3 thresholds, 2 timings, nothing else)
findings.proposed_fix: Add a connected-source guard on the Hardware Thresholds section and add unsafeDebounceSeconds / resumeDelayMinutes to WeatherSettings with rows on this page.

findings.title: The 'No weather data sources available' warning recurs on a completely idle app
findings.what_happened: With weather safety enabled and fail mode Warn Only, the amber 'Weather Safety / No weather data sources available' toast reappeared at 10:00:59, 10:09:20, 10:24:19 and 10:30:22 local while the app sat idle on Settings pages with no run, no equipment and no state change. It is correct information, but as a recurring nag with nothing the user can act on from that toast it trains people to swipe away weather toasts -- which is precisely the class of alert you need them to read.
findings.expected: Emit the warning once per condition transition (or once per run start), and surface the standing condition as a persistent inline row on the Weather Safety page instead of a repeating toast.
findings.repro: Settings > Weather Safety > enable weather safety. Settings > Sequencer > Safety fail mode > Warn Only. Leave the app idle and watch for ~30 min.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/providers/weather_safety_provider.dart:762-776 (shouldShowFailModeWarning -> uiNotificationProvider.showWarning on every evaluation that resolves to preserve)
findings.proposed_fix: Track the last-warned condition in the notifier state and only re-emit when the condition string changes or a run starts.

findings.title: A CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' event has no history anywhere in the app
findings.what_happened: Seconds after the red CRITICAL 'Safe the rig' toast fired, I opened the bell in the title bar. It is a 'Transient Alerts' popover (astronomy transients) and it read 'No active alerts' with a 'View all alerts' link into the transients screen. There is no notification centre, no event history and no log surface in the UI where a rig-safing or other critical event can be reviewed after the toast disappears -- an operator who was asleep has no way to find out what happened without opening the raw text log.
findings.expected: A notification/event history reachable from the same bell (or a second bell), retaining critical and warning notifications for the session with timestamps. The 'Cry wolf' class of defects in this project is precisely about statements the app makes and then discards.
findings.repro: Trigger the CRITICAL toast (Weather Safety > enable, with fail-closed). Immediately click the bell icon in the title bar.
findings.where: title-bar bell wires to the transient-alert popover, not to uiNotificationProvider history
findings.proposed_fix: Persist uiNotificationProvider entries for the session and add a history list to the bell popover, separated from transient astronomy alerts.

verified_correct: Weather-safety <-> sequencer auto-park mirroring holds under attack. I toggled 'Auto-park mount' OFF on the Weather Safety page and immediately checked the OTHER page: Sequencer > 'Park on unsafe weather' had flipped to OFF, and BOTH stores were written (app_settings park_on_unsafe_weather=false AND weather_settings.auto_park_enabled=0). I specifically tried to make the two pages disagree; they did not. Evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-84-ws2.png -> settings-obs-85-seq-park.png.

Safety fail mode round-trips correctly through all three values and its subtitle describes the SELECTED mode, not a generic blurb: 'Treat unavailable safety data as unsafe and park/pause equipment' (Fail Closed) / '...as safe and continue operations' (Fail Open) / 'Continue operations and show a warning when safety data is unavailable' (Warn Only). sqlite safety_fail_mode read failClosed / failOpen / warnOnly after each selection. I also tried selecting a value by clicking the previous item's coordinates to see if the control mis-committed -- it did not commit anything, which is the correct failure. Evidence: settings-obs-13 through -18, -86, -87.

Every transport Test button refuses honestly on empty config instead of claiming success. I pressed all of them with nothing configured and specifically looked for a false green: SMTP -> 'Failed: Email is not configured' plus a persistent red X marker next to the button; Discord -> 'Please enter a Discord webhook URL'; Pushover -> 'Please enter both API key and User key'; cloud sync Test Connection and Push Now -> 'Server URL is required.'; push -> 'No push transport is listening. Start remote access before testing.' None of the five fabricated a success. Evidence: settings-obs-33/34/35/46/81/82.

Observation Log 'Export CSV' with zero rows says 'No observations to export.' rather than writing a zero-row file and reporting success. My first attempt looked like a silent no-op (I screenshotted 4s later and the snackbar had gone) -- re-running with a 1.5s delay showed the honest message, and the source path confirms a distinct branch for backend-changed / error / empty. Evidence: settings-obs-27 (missed the toast) then settings-obs-28 (toast captured).

The TNS Bot API key really does go to the OS keyring and the 'stored securely' claim is verified by read-back, not asserted optimistically. After typing SUPERSECRETTNSKEY123 I grepped the entire scratch profile (grep -r over /tmp/ns-audit/settings-obs) and the app_settings table for the plaintext: zero hits. I then navigated to another settings page and back, forcing initState to re-run its real has() query -- the row came back as 'Stored securely in the keyring. Enter a new value to replace it.' with a masked hint. Evidence: settings-obs-24, settings-obs-25.

Plate Solving is exemplary at reporting a missing dependency: a red 'ASTAP not installed -- Skotiq cannot plate-solve' banner with two download links, a numbered 3-step get-started card, 'Auto-detect -- not found' on both the ASTAP and solve-field executable rows, and 'No ASTAP path to verify. Browse for one above first.' next to a Verify button. Active solver defaults to Auto-fallback (try ASTAP, fall back to Astrometry.net), which is the right default. This is the standard the PHD2 page should be held to. Evidence: settings-obs-64, -66-ps-1, -67.

Numeric and text settings persist to sqlite immediately and correctly. Verified by editing in the UI and then querying the DB within seconds: plate_solve_timeout 60 -> 45, phd2_port 4400 -> 4401, weather_settings row (thresholds + alert distance + lead time), notification_routing_matrix JSON, autosave.sequence_enabled false -> true. No edit was lost and none wrote a different key than the one the row claimed.

The Discord Webhook PLUGIN dialog explicitly disambiguates itself from notification routing -- 'Per-node webhooks ... The URL below is a default/test webhook saved for convenience -- to fire on observatory events instead, use Notification Routing.' This is exactly the disclosure the two duplicate Discord sections on the Notifications page are missing, so the pattern already exists in the codebase. Evidence: settings-obs-91-discord-plugin.png.

'Push critical alerts to mobile' ships ON but its subtitle states the truth without being asked: 'No device has registered for push, and this host has no push delivery configured -- critical alerts will only appear in the app while it is open on your network.' Same pattern on Weather Safety, where auto-park/auto-resume rows append '-- inactive until "Enable weather safety" is on' while the master switch is off, and drop the suffix the moment it is enabled. I watched that suffix appear and disappear live. Evidence: settings-obs-30, settings-obs-06 vs settings-obs-07.

The Annotations page is complete and coherent: Display (enable, labels, magnitudes, max objects slider, grid overlay), Magnitude Filter (min/max sliders), Object Types (six per-type switches each showing Visible/Hidden in the subtitle so state is readable without parsing the switch), Fade Effects (hover/idle opacity, fade duration), Click to Identify (enable + search radius in arcseconds), Marker Styles. Every switch's subtitle restates its state in words. Evidence: settings-obs-69, -70-ann-2, -71-ann-end.
coverage_note:
Drove the real Linux release bundle on :83 with profile settings-obs (--fresh), 130 screenshots under /tmp/ns-audit/shots/settings-obs-*.png, cross-checking the UI against /tmp/ns-audit/settings-obs/data/skotiq.db after every write. My instance (pid 1326944) is stopped; the other agents' instances were left alone.

All eight settings: units in my named scope were visited and operated, not just rendered: weather-safety, sequencer, science, notifications (all seven transports plus the routing matrix), integrations/plugins, annotations, plate-solving, phd2-guiding. Observation log, auto-save and cloud-sync were reached via their real homes (Science > Observation Log; Files & Storage > AUTO-SAVE & BACKUPS; Advanced > Backup & Restore > Backup & Sync) -- note that no settings page is called "Cloud Sync" and searching the settings search box for "cloud" or "sync" does not surface it, which is itself a small discoverability wrinkle I did not raise as a separate finding.

Two honest gaps, both listed in units_unreached: I did not press the MQTT section's Save/Test buttons (I enumerated its fields and edited Topic live), and I did not reach the Home Assistant block at the very tail of the Notifications page -- Home Assistant was covered instead from Settings > Integrations, where its Configure dialog produced finding D5.

Method notes for whoever follows: the settings nav and the detail pane are separate scroll views and neither responds to Page_Down; `DISPLAY=:83 xdotool mousemove X Y click --repeat N 5` (or 4 for up) is the only way to scroll. Two of my early clicks landed on the wrong control because I read a screenshot from an earlier batch than the live scroll position -- always screenshot immediately before a click on a long page. Snackbars last about 4s, so a 4s delay after a button press will show you an empty screen and make an honest message look like a silent no-op (this nearly produced a false finding on Observation Log > Export CSV). Also worth knowing: the scratch profile does NOT isolate everything -- flutter_secure_storage writes to the developer's real login keyring, the checkpoint dir resolves to ~/.local/share/com.skotiq.desktop, and auto-save bundles land in ~/Documents/Skotiq/backups shared with every concurrent agent, so "Recent Backups" mixes profiles (I used the per-profile autosave.last_backup_at key rather than the file list to nail finding D3).

Sections deliberately not touched because they belong to the other two agents sharing the settings area: general, appearance, location, files-storage (beyond the auto-save block), help, about, equipment-profiles, connection, imaging, calibration, calibration-library, dark-library, captured-images, image-grading, adaptive-exposure, adaptive-conditions, autofocus, preflight, catalogs, rig-catalogs, remote-access, backup (beyond Backup & Sync), updates, replay-debug, observing-lists.
